subject: Azimuth11b: temporary fallback routing & customer action items
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Liu <mike@tiltlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 18:32:00 -0800
Subject: Azimuth11b: temporary fallback routing & customer action items

Hi Mike / Tilt team,

Quick update from our side — we observed an elevated rate of timeouts and 5xx responses specifically impacting the Azimuth11b model between ~17:40-18:20 PST. We implemented an automated fallback policy at 18:05 PST that routes new generation requests to the compatible Azimuth11b-quant and Azimuth10b variants to reduce user-facing errors. You may have seen transient increases in latency while the routing change propagated.

What we’ve done so far:
- Activated fallback routing to Azimuth11b-quant and Azimuth10b at 18:05 PST.
- Scoped the impact to requests with seq_len > 1024 and prompt types using long-context streaming.
- Collected KV/cache dumps and crash logs; attaching a trimmed log bundle for your ops team (azimuth11b-logs-20261129.zip).

Immediate customer-facing effects you should expect:
- New requests should succeed more consistently but may return slightly different generation characteristics for a small subset of prompts.
- Ongoing sessions pinned to Azimuth11b might have experienced a dropped response; we’re prioritizing session affinity fixes.

Requested next steps from Tilt: please share any high-priority prompt sets or production examples that you rely on Azimuth11b for — that helps our eval engineers prioritize fidelity checks.

We’ll follow up with a post-incident update once we have a root-cause hypothesis. I’ve cc’d Ben and Lauren from ops and account respectively; Ben is leading the triage.

Attachment: azimuth11b-logs-20261129.zip (zip, ~6MB, trimmed)

Thanks,
Michael Grant

Subject: Azimuth11b triage notes & immediate asks (internal)

Team — quick internal triage notes (summary):
- Symptom: elevated 5xx and timeouts concentrated on Azimuth11b (~17:40–18:20 PST), spike tied to long-context generation paths.
- Impact: affected ~0.9% of customer traffic platform-wide; Tilt Labs reported visible 502s in their dashboards (~3% of their Azimuth11b calls during window).
- Short-term mitigation taken: fallback routing enabled to Azimuth11b-quant and Azimuth10b; rolling restart of 3 serving nodes implicated in the traces.
- Artifacts collected: KV cache snippets, kernel crash logs, perf traces (see Drive link).

Immediate asks:
1) Ben — please validate whether the 3 restarted nodes showed memory pressure or kernel-level OOM at time of failure. Pull dmesg and nvml logs and paste top-level indicators here.
2) Marissa — coordinate a controlled canary (10% traffic) back onto Azimuth11b once we have a small mitigation build; flag any regression automatically to Tilt.
3) Lauren — I'll draft a short customer-facing note (follow-up) confirming recovery window and next-steps. Can you confirm any commercial/credit asks from Tilt?

Im attaching the mitigation checklist we used (azimuth-fallback-checklist.pdf) for your review.

-Michael
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Liu <mike@tiltlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 02:14:00 -0800
Subject: Azimuth11b: recovery confirmed and next steps

Hi Mike,

Final update from our end — we completed a targeted patch and rolling canary starting 23:10 UTC (Nov 29) that addresses a kernel memory regression in the Azimuth11b attention kernel. Key points:
- Recovery: full routing back to Azimuth11b resumed at 01:45 PST (Nov 30) after successful 10% then 50% canary windows with no recurrence of the timeouts.
- Root cause hypothesis: an edge-case in the attention kernel that surfaced with large KV cache sizes; the patch constrains temporary allocations and improves cache eviction heuristics.
- Verification: we validated behavior against Tilt's sample prompts and internal regression suites; no significant fidelity degradation detected for the examples you provided.
- Credits/Comp: if you observed material customer impact beyond noise, Lauren is ready to discuss a credits package — please let her know.

Artifacts and follow-ups:
- Logs and perf traces: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/azimuth11b-logs-20261129
- Incident ticket: RW-INC-2248 (postmortem draft in progress; ETA for full RCA: 72 hours)
- If Tilt prefers, we can schedule a short 30-minute run-through tomorrow to walk the team through the fix and verification steps.

Thanks again for your patience and for sending the sample prompts — they helped prioritize checks.

Best,
Michael Grant
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
